fairness_rules: Advance silhouettes and directional cues before the commitment; no blind lethal pit.

No constant clean lane: far and near blockers cover all lanes; movement and hopping are required. A hit is a failure even if immunity allows survival.
Numbers assume neutral horizontal input at560 scroll; sustained forward+diagonal needs separate witnesses, not an unverified universal-feasibility claim.

depth_contract: Background equipment is attached to visible wall brackets, ceiling rails, pipes or architecture. Show the pivot and full trajectory into the riding plane.
Separate background silhouette, projected target cue, moving attack body, contact-plane collision, broken support rim and below-channel waterfall layers.
Shadow and cue communicate the eventual danger footprint; they cause no damage. Only declared contact phases collide, using both hero heads and full90x28 board support.
Water remains safe where the channel still supports it. A broken channel shows missing structure, a dark drop, fractured edges and continuous falling water, not an unexplained dark water patch.
Destruction persists in world coordinates until the entire hole and visual rim clear the course; no timed healing under a rider. Pause/reset/checkpoint must synchronize geometry, effects and audio.

encounter_composition: Reserve a reachable opposite-bank refuge and its approach/exit. Never combine a head commitment with a hand strike or another obstacle closing that refuge. Reserve the refuge until the entire hole passes, not merely until the head retreats.
Do not attack through an existing jump, island landing or ramp commitment unless a separate full-sequence proof establishes a safe response. Do not invalidate a previously signaled safe landing.

Recurring sightings teach anticipation, lane lock and track damage separately. The final fight combines learned attacks with deliberately reserved recovery windows; isolated showcase three-second rests remain unchanged.
Proposed final encounter is a scrolling chase arena at560 with a curated supply of intact track and fixtures. A fixed arena or speed change is an alternative requiring approval, not assumed.

defeat_options.proposal: Lure a committed bite into a clearly signaled heavy fixture or valve assembly. Recovery exposes a vulnerability or advances environmental defeat.
defeat_options.tradeoff: Fits the existing steering/jump ride without enabling weapons; requires fixtures, hit feedback and a clear reason the fixture hurts or jams the mouth.

defeat_options.proposal: After a missed bite, a visible mouth weak point can be attacked briefly.
defeat_options.tradeoff: Ride currently disables firing; enabling combat, hero weapon parity, boss HP and targeting would need explicit design and implementation approval.

defeat_options.proposal: Survive a finite chase and steer the boss into a prepared environmental trap.
defeat_options.tradeoff: No new shooting loop, but player agency must be clear so victory is more than a hidden timer.

open_decisions.recommendation: Start with baiting a bite into a visible heavy fixture/jam, fitting the existing steering-and-jump ride. Choose exposed-mouth shooting only if enabling ride combat is desired; survival into a trap is the other option.
Use ordinary1HP/shared immunity over intact track; keep early track-bites separate and pit falls lethal. Instant-fatal direct bites need an explicit choice.

Prototype a scrolling chase with the head right/player left and a checkpoint immediately before it; reset destroyed track on retry. Fixed arena, speed changes or new camera projection remain alternatives.
Keep the boss unnamed until Sean selects a name and Storyboarding supplies the characterization; approved visual direction does not need to be chosen again.
Choose from Audio audition candidates separately; generation of auditions does not select runtime mappings.

engineering_assessment.current_renderer: Node2D manually draws a 960x540 scene. Bank position, horizontal travel and jumping height are separate simulation quantities, with authored 2D depth sorting and clipping.
engineering_assessment.true_camera: A Camera2D rotation only rolls the image in its plane; it cannot reveal new side views. True yaw/pitch needs 3D geometry or a new projection/content pipeline and appropriate authored views. Highest scope and regression risk.
engineering_assessment.controlled_2d: A reversible oblique presentation is feasible. Centralize world-to-screen projection for floor geometry, raised actors, shadows, collision outlines, warnings, clipping and culling. Keep HUD/menu coordinates flat. Existing sprite fronts cannot reveal missing sides; Art review is required.
engineering_assessment.controls: Decide and test world-relative versus screen-relative steering before production. Screen-relative controls need the inverse projection; preserve input magnitude, clamp behavior and jump timing. Avoid changing that mapping mid-jump.
engineering_assessment.fairness: Measure projected hazard lead time, lane widths, readable landing areas and visibility at both horizontal clamps. A changed camera must not conceal fatal gaps or shorten warning acceptance silently. Preserve locked attack targets.
engineering_assessment.difficulty: Difficulty-specific tilt is a presentation proposal, not an approved rebalance. Validate both heroes, all difficulties and normal versus hard poses before assigning any angle to a mode.
prototype_options: Lowest scope: fixed small oblique projection in an isolated optional test, with reversible toggle and collision overlay.
Higher scope: smoothly change projection only in safe approach intervals; test motion discomfort and never reinterpret a held input mid-hazard.
Largest scope: true 3D/projection rewrite with new viewpoints, lighting/occlusion and revised assets.
engineering_assessment.recommendation: Next decision: authorize an isolated fixed small oblique 2D projection prototype, with reversible toggle and support overlay, or retain current view. Test lane/landing readability before any animated camera or difficulty-specific angle.
engineering_assessment.implementation_status: Feasibility/source assessment only. No camera projection prototype or camera gameplay changes in Prototype 113.
